q: My cousin, who is a L&D nurse as well as pregnant with her third baby, recommended smooth move tea to me (only once a week). I then looked it up with Claude (AI chat) just to be extra safe and of course AI said to skip it, that it could cause cramping. That freaked me so I haven’t tried it.
c: First-time mum at 11 weeks, constipated since the start.

q: I only use AI as a data point not a diagnostic or dr replacement, same with reddit comments, just a data point to be added for consideration :).
c: Same author in a reply to commenters.

q: I live on the east coast and work in municipal government. It’s in my contract that I have 12 weeks paid maternity leave since I am a full time employee. My job is high stress.
c: Positive test the same day, at about 3.5 weeks.

q: But I am so scared and not prepared for the unknown.
c: Same author; asks how to break the news to her parents.

q: I feel so selfish recently for not being able to be there for people but I feel like I can’t help it. I also feel like people don’t truly understand the weight of my emotions.
c: First pregnancy, past 30 weeks; had to leave a family graduation, overstimulated and crying.

q: I’m taking my prenatals, eating healthy and getting some moderate exercise but my immune system just can’t keep up. I’m so exhausted of being exhausted.
c: First pregnancy, 4 months in, fourth cold in 2.5 months.

q: My husband says to me half way through that they needed to be cooked. I checked and it says ‘ready to heat’ on the packet and I just feel so stupid and irresponsible.
c: 36 weeks with twins (UK), ate a chilled tapas dish straight from the tub.

q: Today I finally hit a wall at 37 weeks. Baby is sitting very low, head down and good to go. I woke up to my toddler freaking out because my husband stalled breakfast too long.
c: Second pregnancy, much harder than her first.

q: I was supposed to have a pregnancy massage tomorrow for mothers day but I’m in so much pain in my hip and pelvis area and today I was miserable so I cancelled.
c: Same author.

q: I seriously cannot imagine going another 3 weeks like this! Especially with a toddler, but thank god for my husband because he helps out tremendously.
c: Same author; asks soon-to-be mums of two about the final weeks.

q: I'm realizing I should have done some preemptive research in case I would continue to get migraines, but a little too late for tonight at least.
c: 7 weeks, a long-standing condition returned and her usual treatment was prescribed before pregnancy.

q: Options where I live are very limited unless I drive 2 hours away. The OB I’ve been seeing has LOTS of patients so I’m constantly having to remind him about things and he never remembers anything about me.
c: 36 weeks, US, feels she isn't taken seriously and it's too late to switch.

q: I feel robbed of these beautiful pregnancy experiences that most women I know have :/
c: Mother of two weighing a third after two pregnancies that each ended in a frightening complication.

q: i feel like shit honestly because i thought i’ll be able to workout during my pregnancy, not to lose weight but at least to stay strong. I do not want to be weak.
c: 7+5 with her second, daughter is 3; eating more is the only thing that eases nausea.

q: i thought i could do the same this time around but i am so much more exhausted this pregnancy. Even just walking for more than 10 minutes makes me extra exhausted.
c: Same author replying to tips.

q: Planned for a natural birth and did all the right things but ended up with an emergency c section and 5 extra days in the hospital
c: Same author on her first birth.

q: seeing the way my husband looked at me when he realized there was nothing coming out was just heart breaking (obviously he wasn't being intentionally malicious in any way) but it can be very draining and disappointing not being able to.
c: Hours after the birth, struggling with latch despite a lactation consultant.

q: Thankfully, it's supposed to go back to normal eventually but I feel like that's something we should be talking about more??
c: Ten days after a birth she calls dreamy; an unexpected body change nobody mentioned.

q: I had my husband look throughout my pregnancy and kept telling him to tell me if I looked different but also don't hurt my feelings lol. The only update I got was "it looks good baby"
c: Same author in a reply.

q: With today being Mother’s Day, we are hosting my family for a lunch. He is suggesting to tell them but I’m feeling nervous of sharing the good news so early and jinxing it.
c: First positive test the day before, about 4 weeks; her husband is thrilled.

q: it would have been helpful if someone had properly briefed me on how it might affect baby, it was absolutely breaking my heart watching her in so much pain last night.
c: UK, nearly three weeks postpartum, breastfeeding while on a prescribed course after a surgical birth.

q: since we haven’t announced it yet, i feel alone other than my hubby of course- but i just want some mom friends or expecting moms friends to talk about what is going on!!
c: 24, first pregnancy, 8 weeks, keeping it quiet for now.

q: “Oh my goodness my water broke! \*proceeds to show a pool of liquid on the floor\* Let’s rush to the hospital. I’m in so much pain but I’m going to do these breathing exercises. Ohh look the baby is crowning. PUSHHH. Yay baby is here, all done now.”
c: New mum mocking how TV shows labour.

q: Hahaa meanwhile it’s a roller coaster of both emotions and pain. And lots of blood/cleanup.
c: Same author.

q: I was upset by this and he said that after the pregnancy I would go back to normal and things between us would go back to normal too. Later I brought it up again that I was disturbed by what he said, and he reiterated that after the pregnancy things would be different and told me to “get a grip”.
c: 8 months pregnant; husband more or less admitted he is no longer attracted to her.

q: I worry that his postpartum expectations are unrealistic. I will be recovering from birth, perhaps have scars and so on. My looks will hardly get better from here.
c: Same author.

q: I am a Sahm and I literally couch rot every day because I feel sick and I don’t have the energy to do anything. It breaks my heart that I can’t play with my toddler the way I used to.
c: 9 weeks with an unexpected second, toddler is 22 months.

q: My first pregnancy wasn’t this rough. I somehow had 0 symptoms my first trimester and then got hit with 3-4 weeks of nausea and that was it.
c: Same author.

q: 15 weeks today and i definitely feel a lot better! The nausea has subsided almost completely.
c: Same author's follow-up five weeks later.

q: I don’t know what’s normal, I don’t remember what it was like with my son even though he’s only 3. I just remember I wasn’t anxious about these things PP.
c: The day after her second birth, frightened something will go wrong with her own body.

q: We are told this is a beautiful time, Part of natures course, It’s what women are made for, But grief has made a home inside me too.
c: A poem posted at 12 weeks about losing the life she expected.

q: Now I count symptoms instead of memories. I count weeks instead of adventures.
c: Same poem.
